title: The Circulation Desk: access-route registry

sources.R01: research/R01-open-books.md (Free and open-access books; 55-book coverage test), 2026-10-15
sources.catalog: catalog.json: Open Library works (CC0), fetched October 2026

A1.name: Author- or publisher-hosted full text
A1.d: A complete text the author or publisher deliberately makes available. Terms range from Creative Commons to "personal use only"; each route quotes them.

A2.name: Open-access book (DOAB)
A2.d: Listed in the Directory of Open Access Books with an open licence.

A3.name: Public domain: Project Gutenberg
A3.d: The work has a Project Gutenberg ebook id. Free to read and reuse in the US.

A4.name: Standard Ebooks edition
A4.d: A proofread, typeset public-domain edition from Standard Ebooks.

A5.name: Open scan on the Internet Archive
A5.d: Open Library marks the work "public": a full scan anyone can read without a loan.

A6.name: Partial free text
A6.d: Only part of the book is free. Counted as a start, not as the book.

B1.name: Internet Archive loan, English scan verified
B1.d: An English-language scan is in the Internet Archive lending collection. Free account; 1-hour renewable loans, some 14-day; waitlists possible.

B2.name: Internet Archive loan flag, edition unverified
B2.d: Open Library flags the work "borrowable", but the flag is a maximum over all editions, translations included, so the lendable copy may not be in English.

B3.name: Translation-only lending (not routed)
B3.d: The only lendable scans are translations or study guides; English scans are print-disabled only. Shown as a warning, never as a route.

P1.name: Print-disabled access only
P1.d: The scan is available only to readers certified as print-disabled (through a qualifying organization or a certifying professional). Offered only when the reader says they are eligible.

L1.name: Library ebook, holdings checked
L1.d: Libby holdings at named libraries on the snapshot date, with copies and holds where recorded. Wait estimate: two weeks per loan cycle, holds ÷ copies cycles.

L2.name: Library ebook, likely (not checked)
L2.d: Not checked for this title. In R03, Bay Area Libby held 16 of 20 humanities and 18 of 33 technical titles; popular trade books are held most often.

O1.name: O'Reilly catalog, title checked
O1.d: Present (or absent) in O'Reilly's public book sitemap.

O2.name: O'Reilly, estimated from the publisher
O2.d: Not checked by title. Estimated from the publisher's share of the sitemap: Wiley ≈9,200, O'Reilly ≈9,000, Pearson ≈6,200, Apress ≈4,000, CRC ≈3,000, Manning ≈1,100; MIT Press, Cambridge, Oxford and core Springer 0.

O3.name: O'Reilly through a public library
O3.d: SFPL, Oakland, Berkeley, San José and Santa Clara County libraries offer O'Reilly for Public Libraries to cardholders. About 70% that sitemap titles are readable this way.

E1.name: Perlego, title checked (US rights)
E1.d: Present (or absent) in Perlego with US sales rights. "Restricted" titles probably need the Complete plan.

E2.name: Perlego, estimated from the publisher
E2.d: Not checked by title. Perlego carries Routledge (153k), CRC (34k), Wiley (19k), Cambridge (15.7k), Princeton (9.8k), MIT Press (1k); almost no O'Reilly (33) and no Pearson.

V1.name: Everand, unverified
V1.d: Everand's catalog blocked automated checks. Plans give 1, 3 or 5 unlocks a month. Routed for popular trade titles only, as an estimate.

K1.name: Kindle Unlimited, unverified
K1.d: Claims "over 5 million digital titles"; price about $11.99 unverified. No title on this list was checked, so the desk routes nothing through it.

U1.name: Buy, price checked
U1.src: R03 §1.5 (AbeBooks, cheapest total incl. US shipping, 2026-10-15)
U1.d: Cheapest AbeBooks listing by ISBN on the snapshot date. Ships in about 3–5 days.

U2.name: Buy, price not checked
U2.d: Always possible, but no price was recorded. Search by ISBN.

H1.name: Free shadow
H1.d: Free material covering similar ground, such as a course by the same department. A judgement, not an edition of the book.

X1.name: No shadow libraries
X1.d: The desk never routes to unauthorised copies, even when nothing else is free.

keys.name: Open web
keys.note: Author sites, open-access books, Project Gutenberg, Standard Ebooks, open Internet Archive scans.

keys.name: Internet Archive account
keys.note: Controlled digital lending: 1-hour renewable loans, some 14-day; up to 10 books at a time.

keys.name: San Francisco PL card
keys.friction: Free to California residents; apply online, show ID in person
keys.note: Libby, O'Reilly for Public Libraries, ProQuest eBook Central, JSTOR (remote access disputed).

keys.name: Bay Area card stack
keys.friction: Five free cards (Oakland, Berkeley, San José, Santa Clara County, Peninsula); several visits
keys.note: Libby at five more systems; O'Reilly at Oakland, Berkeley, San José and Santa Clara County.

keys.name: LA Public Library card
keys.friction: Free to Californians, in person in LA (e-card for LA City residents only)
keys.note: Libby with MIT Press ebooks no Bay Area library had (CLRS, Goodfellow, Sutton & Barto). No O'Reilly.

keys.name: O'Reilly Individual
keys.note: Strong on Wiley, O'Reilly, Pearson, Packt, Apress, CRC, Manning; no MIT Press, Cambridge, Oxford or core Springer. Terms forbid using content as AI input.

keys.name: Perlego Complete
keys.friction: $27 a month, $199 a year (Essential $15 lacks "restricted" titles)
keys.note: Humanities and social science: Routledge, CRC, Cambridge, Princeton, Yale, Chicago. Almost no O'Reilly or Pearson.

keys.name: Everand Plus
keys.note: Unlock model since the unlimited plan ended. Catalog could not be checked; routes are estimates.

keys.name: Kindle Unlimited
keys.note: No title on this list was checked against it, so it opens nothing here.

keys.name: Print-disabled eligibility
keys.friction: Not for sale: certification of a print disability is required
keys.note: Unlocks print-disabled scans on the Internet Archive for eligible readers only. The advisor never recommends it.

explanations.tfs: The catalog says "borrowable", but that flag comes from translations: the English scan is print-disabled only, so the desk does not offer an Internet Archive loan [B3]. The realistic route is a library ebook. SFPL had 13 copies and 51 holds on the snapshot date, roughly an eight-week wait; LAPL's queue was longer [L1].
explanations.geron: Tonight's free route is an Internet Archive loan, but of the 1st edition (2017, TensorFlow 1) [B1]. For the current 3rd edition, O'Reilly carries it [O1], and a library card reaches O'Reilly at no cost [O3]; San José and Santa Clara County also hold Libby copies [L1].
explanations.scott: No free copy and no English loan: the Internet Archive scan is print-disabled only [P1]. Perlego carries the Yale edition with US rights [E1], so a month of Perlego opens it tonight. A library ebook is plausible but was not checked by title [L2].
explanations.esl: The authors host a PDF of the 2nd edition [A1]. Their server reset connections during the October check, so an English Internet Archive loan of the 1st edition is listed as the backup [B1]. Neither O'Reilly nor Perlego carries it [O1] [E1].
explanations.jaynes: Only chapters 1–3 are free, as a 95-page PDF on the editor's site [A6]. The full book is not in O'Reilly, Perlego or any library R03 checked [O1] [E1] [L1], so after the free chapters the route is a used copy, about $70 on the snapshot date [U1].
explanations.ddia: Not free: the author's site points to purchase. O'Reilly carries both editions [O1], and a public library card reaches O'Reilly at no cost [O3]. SFPL also held 10 Libby copies [L1].

tray.explanation: This is Judgment under Uncertainty: Heuristics and Biases, edited by Kahneman, Slovic and Tversky; the local catalog lists it as "Judgement under uncertainty" (OL12970183W). Open Library has no ebook for it, so there is no Internet Archive route. Its ISBN is a Cambridge one, and O'Reilly carries no Cambridge titles [O2]; Perlego carries about 15,700, so it may be there, unchecked [E2]. Otherwise, buy a copy [U2].
